newsitem.title: THAILAND: Amnuay says baht stabilises on higher liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Amnuay says baht stabilises on higher liquidity.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Thursday the baht has stabilised this week on higher liquidity in the local money market which pushed down Thai interbank rates.

The minister told reporters that state-owned Government Savings Bank has been an active participant in the Thai interbank market and its role has helped the government regulate money supply and curb speculation against the baht.
"The overnight interbank rate has eased to 11 percent, a reasonable level," he said, comparing with 25 percent late last week.

Senior finance ministry official Nipat Pukkanasut said the government has asked state-owned Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) not to use surplus funds and resources in its bonds portfolio to speculate in the domestic market when interbank rates are volatile.
He said EGAT is a large state enterprise normally carrying large surplus funds and its trading in the local market could further aggravate its volatility.
